newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Malaysia to sell new 20,000-bpd crude in July.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to sell new 20,000-bpd crude in July.

text.p: Malaysia is to start sales of a medium sweet crude in July, rich in gas oil and low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR), industry sources said on Thursday.
The Kekwa blend will start production at 20,000 barrels per day (bpd) to provide the first cargo of 300,000 to 350,000 barrels. They said production would rise by 1999 to 50,000 bpd.
The crude has an American Petroleum Institute (API) gravity of 36 degrees and sulphur content of 0.04 percent, the sources said.
The gas oil and LSWR yields are 40 percent each, they said.
Initial marketing will be on a spot basis using Tapis as a benchmark. One source said the crude is likely to trade at a discount to Tapis -- Asia's benchmark for light sweet grades.
The offshore Kekwa blend is produced from the field in the Commercial Arrangement Area between Malaysia and Vietnam.

The consortium developing the field is Petronas Carigali, the exploration arm of Petronas, with 46.06 percent, PetroVietnam Exploration and Production with 12.5 percent, Canada's International Petroleum Corp (IPC) with 26.44 percent and Sands Petroleum AB SAPEfb.S with 15 percent.
